original_target.title: A roughening transition in the three-dimensional Ising model

full_original_statement:
For $`\beta>0`$, consider the nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model on $`\mathbb Z^3`$ at zero field. Its Gibbs laws have, in every finite $`\Lambda`$, conditional probabilities proportional to

```math
\exp\!\left(\beta\!\!\sum_{\{x,y\}:\ |x-y|_1=1,\ \{x,y\}\cap\Lambda\ne\varnothing}\sigma_x\sigma_y\right),\qquad \sigma_x\in\{-1,1\},
```

with the spins outside $`\Lambda`$ fixed. Let $`\beta_c(3)=\inf\{\beta:\mu_\beta^+(\sigma_0)>0\}`$, where $`\mu_\beta^+`$ is the limit with all-plus boundary condition.

Does there exist $`\beta_R>\beta_c(3)`$ such that every Gibbs law is translation invariant for $`\beta_c(3)<\beta<\beta_R`$, while a Gibbs law that is not translation invariant exists for every $`\beta>\beta_R`$?

sources.scope_comparison: The exact target is an interval beta_c<beta<beta_R on which every infinite-volume Gibbs law is translation invariant, followed by existence of nontranslation-invariant laws for every beta>beta_R. The2026 primary body studies a finite transverse slab/compactification and numerical tensor-network fixed points and estimated transition temperatures. It does not classify all3D Gibbs states or prove the asserted threshold quantifiers. Low-temperature rigidity supplies only a restricted regime. No matching complete rigorous announcement was found.
